title: Local finite-field normal form for norm-algebraic-closure cocycles
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended norm topology, a finite intermediate extension $E$, a profinite group $G$, and a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W$ with continuous $E$-linear $G$-action [def-pod-l-adic-representations]. Give $V_F=F\otimes_E W$ its finite-dimensional product topology for each intermediate $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, including $F=\Omega$; $G$ acts through $W$ and trivially on $F$. For a topological group $J$ and a topological $E$-vector space $V$ with continuous linear $J$-action define the ordinary nonnegative complex $C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=C(J^n,V)$ of abstract $E$-vector spaces, with $C^0_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=V$ and differential
$$(df)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
For $n=0$ this reads $(dv)(g)=gv-v$. Cohomology means kernel modulo image in abstract $E$-vector spaces, with no closure of the coboundaries. For every integer $n\geq1$ and every $z\in C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_\Omega)$ with $dz=0$, there exist an open subgroup $H\subseteq G$, a finite intermediate extension $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, a continuous cocycle $u\in C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V_F)$, and a continuous cochain $b\in C^{n-1}_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V_\Omega)$ such that
$$z|_{H^n}=u+db$$
after the specified inclusion $V_F\hookrightarrow V_\Omega$. Here open means open in the profinite topology; no finite generation, finite cohomological dimension, completeness of $\Omega$, or discrete topology on $W$ is assumed. This is solely a statement about explicit continuous functions, with no identification with condensed derived invariants.

proof.text:
Choose an $E$-basis of $W$ of size $d$, identifying the specified coefficient spaces with $L^d$ for $E\subseteq L\subseteq\Omega$. The action matrices lie in $E$. By [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates], the function
$$f(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=g_0z(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n)$$
is continuous, diagonally equivariant and satisfies $\delta f=\Psi_{n+1}(dz)=0$. The coefficient actions are jointly continuous: each matrix entry is a continuous coordinate of $g e_j$, and each output coordinate is a finite sum of products of entries and vector coordinates.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-map-finite-field-rectangle] to this $f$ with $m=n+1$ to obtain $F$, $H$ and $a_0,\ldots,a_n$ with $f(Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n)\subseteq F^d$. Its hypotheses hold because $G$ is profinite and $n+1\geq1$; no cocycle property is needed for this application.

source.place: Paragraph (3), arithmetic local cocycle input; repair assembly step 2.

proof.text: Choose the continuous $E$-linear scalar retraction $p_F:\Omega\to F$ by [lem-sfb-finite-subfield-continuous-linear-retraction]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-scalar-cochain-retraction] with $L=\Omega$ to get $P:\Omega^d\to F^d$, inclusion $i$ and $Q=1-iP$. Thus $r=Qf$ is a continuous equivariant homogeneous cocycle vanishing on the rectangle. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-cocycle-rectangle-detection], since $n\geq1$ and $H$ is open, there is a continuous $H$-equivariant $t:H^n\to\Omega^d$ with $r|_{H^{n+1}}=\delta t$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), arithmetic local cocycle input; repair assembly step 3.

proof.text:
Put $u=(Pz)|_{H^n}$ and $b=\Phi_{n-1}t$, explicitly
$$b(h_1,\ldots,h_{n-1})=t(1,h_1,h_1h_2,\ldots,h_1\cdots h_{n-1}).$$
By [lem-sfb-finite-scalar-cochain-retraction], $u$ is continuous with values in $F^d$ and $du=P(dz)|_{H^{n+1}}=0$. Apply $\Phi_n$ to $Qf|=\delta t$ using coefficient and restriction naturality and $\Phi_n\delta=d\Phi_{n-1}$ from [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates]. This gives $z|_{H^n}-iu=db$, as required. For $n=1$, $b=t(1)$; rank zero, the trivial group and non-normal $H$ are included.

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause match. Ω is an uncompleted NormedField with NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] and IsAlgClosure, so its norm is the unique extended norm. E is a finite IntermediateField; G is a ProfiniteGrp; hρ = IsContinuousCoefficient, the dep's clause (2). The spaces Ω⊗W and F⊗W carry moduleTopology, i.e. the product topology. The differential uses Fin.contractNth with signs (−1)^(j+1), identical to Mathlib inhomogeneousCochains.d (contractNth read at Tuple/Basic.lean:1273). Degree n+1 covers every degree ≥1; for n=1, b is a vector and db = gb−b. The conclusion has an OpenSubgroup H, a finite F with cocycle u in F⊗W, a continuous b, and z|H = incl(u)+db with incl the canonical TensorProduct.map.
